transcript.text: fridge part freezin stuff, lettuce + yoghurts frozen solid at the back. hotpoint ff. any ideas pls

That sounds like the fridge compartment is getting too cold, which usually happens for one of three reasons: the temperature control is set too high, food is blocking airflow by touching the cold back wall, or there's a defrost issue causing ice to build up. Let's rule out the simple stuff first. Please check if your thermostat dial is on its coldest setting (it should be around 3-5°C) and ensure no items are pressed directly against the rear panel where the cold air comes from.
dial is on max/coldest, kids prob moved it. and yeah the fridge is rammed after big shop, stuff pressed against the vent slots at the back

Since the dial was on max and the fridge is packed tight against the vents, that explains why the food froze solid—cold air couldn't circulate and hit the items directly. First, please move everything away from the back wall so there's a gap for airflow, and turn the thermostat down to a mid-range setting (around 3–5°C). Please do a full manual defrost by unplugging the fridge and leaving doors open until all ice is gone; let me know if you found any significant ice build-up behind the rear panel.
turned dial to middle + cleared the vents. after 2 days its better but 1 yoghurt still froze at the very back. is that normal? haven't done the full defrost tho

It is not normal for food to freeze solid after two days with the dial in the middle and vents clear; that suggests a deeper issue than just over-packing. The most likely cause now is a defrost system fault, where ice builds up on the internal evaporator coils (behind the back panel) and blocks airflow, causing localised freezing even when the rest of the fridge is fine. To separate this from a simple thermostat error, you need to see if the ice clears permanently after a full manual defrost. Please switch it off at the socket, leave doors open until all ice has melted (this may take 24 hours), dry it thoroughly, and switch it back on. Let me know if you found significant ice behind the panel.
ok but its only 1 yoghurt right at the very back, rest is fine now. do i really need to do the full defrost? it's a frost-free so thought it did that itself

Yes, you do need to do the full manual defrost. Frost-free fridges only remove ice from the hidden evaporator coils behind the back panel; they cannot clear a blockage if it has already formed there. Please switch it off at the socket, leave doors open for 24 hours until all ice melts, dry it thoroughly, then switch it back on and set the dial to mid-range. Let me know if you find significant ice build-up behind that rear panel.
ok will do the defrost then. how long before I can put food back in once its switched back on?

You can put the food back as soon as the fridge is fully dry and switched back on; there is no need to wait for it to cool down first. However, please ensure all ice has melted during that 24-hour period—this is crucial because if there is still a block of ice behind the rear panel, it will just refreeze and cause the freezing problem again once the compressor starts.
